**Adapter placement controls which transformations can change.** Adding LoRA only to query and value projections is a compact starting point: queries influence what attention looks for, and values influence what information it passes onward. But a task may also require changes to keys, output projections, or the feed-forward transformations that process each token. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685)

**Use a task-based intuition.** A modest style adaptation may work with a small set of attention adapters. A substantial domain or reasoning adaptation may benefit from broader coverage, including MLP layers. This is a hypothesis to test, not a universal mapping from task name to optimal layer set.

For a fixed rank, adding more target matrices increases trainable parameter count, optimizer state, and adapter computation. Comparing Q/V-only rank 64 with all-linear rank 64 is therefore not a matched-budget experiment. Consider either equal parameter budget or explicitly report the extra capacity.

**A useful experiment sequence.** Establish the frozen/SFT baseline, try a small targeted configuration, broaden coverage while measuring held-out gains, and inspect regressions on general tasks. Track peak training memory and inference overhead in merged and unmerged modes. Rank, adapter scale, dropout, learning rate, and data quality interact with placement.

“Most benefit” should mean benefit per relevant resource under your workload, not whichever configuration has the highest raw score after using more parameters. Also verify module names in the actual implementation; model families package fused projections differently, and a pattern-based adapter injector can silently target fewer or different layers than intended.

**Technical details and references.**

There is no universal best LoRA target set. Updating only query/value projections is cheap and can work well when attention adaptation dominates the task. Updating all attention projections and MLP projections gives more capacity to change representations and often helps harder domain adaptation, at higher optimizer/activation cost. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14314)

$$P_{adapter}=r(d_{in}+d_{out})\quad\text{per adapted linear layer}.$$

Choose targets, rank, scaling, and training data jointly. Compare on a held-out task set, including retention of general capabilities, rather than training loss alone. A rank budget spread across many layers differs from the same number of parameters concentrated in a few. Mergeability, quantized-base precision, adapter switching, and inference kernel support are additional practical constraints. Report the exact target module names to make results reproducible.
